office_does: The Pierce County Prosecuting Attorney decides which crimes to charge and prosecutes them, and serves as the county's civil legal counsel.
race_blurb: With Prosecutor Mary Robnett retiring, her Chief Criminal Deputy Coreen Schnepf faces former Superior Court Judge Bryan Chushcoff. Both run on enforcement; Chushcoff targets the office's charging and backlog numbers, while Schnepf runs on her trial record and continuity.

candidates.summary: Chief Criminal Deputy in the Pierce County Prosecutor's Office and a 20-year trial prosecutor, endorsed by outgoing Prosecutor Mary Robnett.
highlights: Chief Criminal Deputy since 2024; earlier led the Domestic Violence and Human Trafficking Unit and prosecuted in Kitsap County [S2]
Would add focus on stolen cars and organized retail theft and build digital-evidence capacity [S3]
Endorsed by Robnett, Legislative District Democrats, Mainstream Republicans, WEA and three IAFF locals [S4][S6]

safety.basis: Runs on violent-crime convictions and more focus on car and retail theft; an endorser also describes a compassionate approach, and no diversion position is stated.

experience.basis: Twenty-year career prosecutor and current chief criminal deputy, running as the incumbent-backed successor and 'next generation of leadership'; first run for office.

candidates.summary: Former Pierce County Superior Court judge (28 years, per his campaign), running on fixing the office's charging rates, felony filings and case backlog.
highlights: Says he served seven terms as a Superior Court judge, including two terms as presiding judge [S2]
Cites the decline-to-charge rate rising from 8% of bookings (2019) to 15.3% (2024) and a growing felony backlog [S3]
Would advocate for more funding to retain experienced staff and reorganize the office [S1]
Endorsed by the Pierce County Republican Party and the Tacoma Police Union [S4][S5]

safety.basis: Calls the rising rate of arrests ending without charges and the falling felony filings failures to correct, pledges to support law enforcement, and is backed by police unions.

experience.basis: Campaign cites 28 years and seven elected terms on the Superior Court plus court leadership roles, presented as proven leadership (not independently verified).

spending.basis: Pairs performance management and measurable outcomes with a call for more funding to retain staff.
